text_blocks.snippet: To apply for a US tourist visa (B1/B2), you'll need several key documents: a valid passport, the DS-160 confirmation page, a visa fee payment receipt, a photo, and potentially an interview appointment letter and supporting documents. You'll also need to demonstrate proof of funds, ties to your home country, and the purpose of your visit.
snippet_highlighted_words: a valid passport, the DS-160 confirmation page, a visa fee payment receipt, a photo, and potentially an interview appointment letter and supporting documents

list.title: Valid Passport:
list.snippet: Make sure your passport is valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay in the US.

list.title: DS-160 Confirmation Page:
list.snippet: This is the confirmation page from your online nonimmigrant visa application (DS-160).

list.title: Visa Fee Payment Receipt:
list.snippet: You'll need proof that you've paid the required visa application fee.

list.title: Photograph:
list.snippet: You'll need a recent digital photo that meets specific US visa requirements. Typically, this means a 2x2 inch photo with a white background.

list.title: Interview Appointment Letter:
list.snippet: If an interview is required, you'll need to bring the appointment confirmation.

text_blocks.snippet: Supporting Documents (May be requested during the interview):

list.title: Proof of Funds:
list.snippet: Evidence that you can financially support yourself during your trip, such as bank statements or asset information.

list.title: Ties to Home Country:
list.snippet: Documents that demonstrate your strong ties to your home country, such as employment verification, property ownership, or family documents.

list.title: Purpose of Visit:
list.snippet: Documents that support your reason for visiting the US, such as an itinerary, hotel reservations, or an invitation letter.

list.title: Previous US Travel Documents:
list.snippet: If you have previously traveled to the US, you may need to provide documentation of those trips.

list.title: Old Passports:
list.snippet: You may need to bring any old passports that show your travel history.

list.title: SEVIS Fee:
list.snippet: If you are applying for an exchange visitor visa (J-1), you may also need to pay the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) fee.

list.title: Interview:
list.snippet: Depending on your situation, you may be required to attend an interview at the US embassy or consulate.

list.title: Dependents:
list.snippet: If you are traveling with family members, they will also need to submit their own visa applications.
